candidates.label: Thessaloniki (historic center)
candidates.support: Thessaloniki has been continuously inhabited on this site since its Hellenistic founding and is undisputed as ancient Thessalonica. Wikidata's point for the modern city center lies about 1.9 km from Pleiades' representative point for the ancient city, a difference consistent with the two datasets marking different features (modern city centroid versus ancient walled city) within a large, continuously occupied urban area.

summary.text: Thessalonica was the capital of the Roman province of Macedonia and a major port on the Via Egnatia. Paul founded a church there on his second missionary journey, later writing 1 and 2 Thessalonians to its believers.
